A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCALE with matching authors, method, and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world robot evaluations in Tables 1–5, alongside original ablations, latency measurements, and uncertainty analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and real-world results and adds numerical hyperparameter sensitivity results in Table 13.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the dual-reference uncertainty score, adaptive action sampling, and visual attention modulation using previous-step uncertainty deviations. Backbone-specific token handling and implementation adaptations also match between v1 Appendix H and v2 Appendix G.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained: LIBERO, SIMPLER-WidowX, LIBERO-PRO-Long with the same four evaluated perturbation types, and the same three ID and two OOD real-world tasks. The new sensitivity tests use existing LIBERO-Long coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: RoboMonkey, TACO, MG-Select, greedy decoding, temperature sampling, top-k, and top-p. The uncertainty-proxy comparisons and two-step oracle comparison are also retained.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix L introduces one-parameter-at-a-time evaluations of T0, alpha, and kappa for OpenVLA and pi0-FAST, fixing other parameters at their main-experiment values. Existing benchmark protocols, training budgets, default settings, and episode counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 13 adds targeted sensitivity analyses of action temperature, temporal smoothing, and attention modulation strength across two backbones, including degradation at excessive kappa. Existing ablations, oracle validation, latency analyses, and case studies remain. The epsilon analysis moves from v1 Appendix B to v2 Appendix L without changing its results.

E5.justification: v1 already reports averaging simulation results over three seeds. v2 Table 12 first supplies standard deviations for the OpenVLA and pi0-FAST LIBERO results, retaining the means and three-seed count. This extends uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs or adding significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 13 adds hyperparameter-dependent success rates, including 39.8% for OpenVLA and 74.4% for pi0-FAST at kappa=3.0. Main Tables 1–8 and the matched oracle, epsilon, baseline-sensitivity, and per-task results retain their values. Table 12 repeats the original LIBERO means with newly reported standard deviations.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and assumptions are retained. The uncertainty derivation and probabilistic interpretation move from v1 Appendices C–D to v2 B–C; baseline uncertainty definitions move from K to J. No new proof or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free, verifier-free, single-pass adaptation of perception and action using self-uncertainty, with improved VLA performance. The added code link and supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.1 strengthens the interpretation of unchanged component ablations from complementarity to synergy through a coupled feedback loop. Appendix L adds explanations linking temperature sensitivity to tokenization and excessive kappa to weakened visual grounding. Appendix K newly interprets the reported standard deviations as evidence of seed stability.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public SCALE code-repository link and states that hyperparameters were selected using LIBERO-Long and reused elsewhere without adjustment. This newly documents selection and access information; hardware, training configurations, token handling, and default hyperparameters were already provided in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to TTS, uncertainty estimation, and visual attention research are retained. Changes to Fang et al.'s title, Breiman's publication year, and Bagnell's initials are bibliographic corrections. Active Inference remains the conceptual motivation.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites experimental setup and analysis paragraphs, adds acknowledgements, and updates affiliation and proceedings text. It moves the epsilon discussion into an expanded sensitivity appendix and adds a statistical-reliability appendix. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–13 for uncertainty reporting and parameter sensitivity, while relocating the old epsilon table as Table 14. Figure 2 receives modest diagram adjustments, Figures 3–4 receive expanded captions, and tables and figures reflow. Existing plotted results and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through LIBERO standard deviations, tuning and code-access disclosures, and sensitivity results that expose failure at excessive attention bounds. These make the retained results easier to assess. The stronger synergy explanation relies on unchanged Table 6 without variability estimates for the individual component gains, so its mechanistic interpretation remains less secure. Overall, the additions provide a useful but limited quality improvement.
